title: Weekly POC regression scrub & prompt curation — Helion Logistics
summary: Weekly POC sync to triage regressions on the pilot scorecard. Discussed a new failure mode in entity extraction, tuned a few guardrail rules that were overblocking, agreed on a focused benchmark run on dedicated capacity, and set next steps for prompt set curation and a deeper on-prem architecture review.
next_steps: Marcus to run 1k-case regression on dedicated pool with seq len sampling and deliver results by 2025-03-26
Samira to send updated pilot pricing + addendum for extra dedicated hours by 2025-03-21
Customer to share 200 additional labelled prompts and two failing cases sets by 2025-03-24
Schedule on-prem deep dive with infra team (SE+Customer SREs) for 2025-03-28
action_items: Marcus Lee: run regression across prompt set A and B, include KV cache off/on matrix — due 2025-03-26
Samira Patel: email pilot addendum and per-token breakdown (with burst capacity pricing) — due 2025-03-21
Priya Menon: export and share 200 labeled examples + edge-case notes — due 2025-03-24
Ethan Zhao: collect SRE requirements and network diagram for VPC deployment — due 2025-03-25
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jensen (Redwood CSM), Priya (Helion ML Lead), Carlos (Helion Product), Ethan (Helion SRE), Marta (Data Analyst), Tom (CTO)

[00:00] Samira: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um lets get started, we've got about 45 minutes. quick round robin if anyone new — oh right, Tom joined, thanks for coming in.
[00:22] Tom: hey all, yeah just listening in, want to make sure the exec level concerns are covered — uptime, cost, and compliance, mostly.
[00:35] Priya: thanks, yeah we're mostly focused on the regression spikes we saw last week when we increased throughput. we got a few examples where entity extraction dropped off.
[00:48] Marcus: mm hm, saw that in the heatmap — there were two clusters: one was long sequences with nested addresses, other was templates with unusual punctuation that confused the parser.
[01:05] Carlos: to be specific, our NPS prompt family — the bot that parses shipment_notes — started dropping 12% on entity recall for certain carriers.
[01:20] Jensen: and that aligns with the scorecard where precision was fine but recall dipped, so the guardrail that was supposed to block hallucinations started overblocking?
[01:33] Marcus: yes exactly, we tuned a strict ner-filter in the guardrail. since it was scoring low confidence it defaulted to redaction and that created a false positive.
[01:45] Priya: right — so for our use case recall matters more than conservative redaction. we need to loosen that rule in the threshold.
[01:58] Samira: ok let's walk through concrete examples. Marta can you read one of the failing snippets?
[02:10] Marta: sure, here's case 1 — "Pickup: 12-04, route: WKT-34, cust: Acme Co., st: 5B, bay-3" the model returned nothing for 'cust' in multiple runs.
[02:25] Marcus: hmm yeah I see, the tokenization on short forms like 'cust' is being treated as low confidence because of the punctuation sequence.
[02:37] Ethan: we actually pushed a throughput bump on Tuesday — is kv cache being warmed properly across pods?
[02:45] Marcus: we think cache warming is intermittent in the hosted test window, yes. but preliminary logs show cache hits are lower for these short-form tokens in the dedicated sim.
[02:58] Carlos: is this an inference runtime bug or prompt design? we need to understand the root cause.
[03:10] Marcus: it's a mix. prompt context matters — longer system priming reduces the issue — but also the guardrail threshold is overly aggressive on low-confidence segments.
[03:25] Samira: proposal: for the next run, we relax that particular ner guardrail threshold for the shipment_notes family, and run a 1k sample on dedicated with cache-on and cache-off to measure delta.
[03:40] Priya: yes and include a seq length stratified sample — short, medium, and long.
[03:50] Marcus: noted. also we'll instrument per-token confidence and send the per-prompt trace so you can eyeball where it crosses the guardrail.
[04:02] Marta: quick Q: will that reduce safety? we're worried loosening will increase hallucination.
[04:10] Jensen: good point — tradeoff. we'll add an extra post-check rule to re-run high-risk outputs through a reranker model to ensure we don't emit bad entities.
[04:22] Marcus: yes, reranker can be a cheaper smaller model to verify before commit. we can toggle it for only those templates.
[04:32] Tom: what's the expected latency impact of reranker?
[04:36] Marcus: minimal in dedicated — about 30 to 60 ms per request if we use a distilled reranker, it's parallelizable.
[04:44] Tom: okay acceptable if it prevents bad writes.
[04:48] Samira: okay next up: prompt set curation, Priya sent us a new batch last night — we flagged 22 edge cases, Marcus flagged 7 that consistently fail.
[05:00] Priya: yes, those 7 are the ones with nested addresses plus emoji in notes.
[05:08] Marcus: emoji breaks a lot of tokenizers, we'll add a normalize pre-step to strip or map emoji to text.
[05:16] Marta: some of our customers actually rely on emoji for quick status updates, can't remove entirely. maybe mapping is better.
[05:24] Marcus: agreed, map to short tokens. we'll include that in the preproc and note it in the traces.
[05:32] Carlos: on scoring, we saw the delta in F1 mainly — so maybe adjust scoring weights to emphasize recall for shipment extraction.
[05:40] Jensen: yes change the pipeline scorecard weight: recall 0.6, precision 0.3, guardrail violations 0.1 for those templates.
[05:50] Priya: that would surface regressions that matter to product.
[05:55] Samira: okay we'll update the scorecard config and push it to the dashboard, you'll see the new columns.
[06:05] Marta: another oddity: some false positives came from vendor names being concatenated, e.g., 'DHL-FR(via)'. model splits that weirdly.
[06:17] Marcus: we can add vendor token normalization too. I'll include a mapping file for common carriers.
[06:24] Ethan: from infra side, we need to verify the dedicated pool size — current pilot config is 2 gpus, at peak we saw queuing. can we get a temporary burst?
[06:35] Samira: yes Samira: we can request temporary burst capacity for the next run, Marcus please include performance numbers so we can justify the burst.
[06:45] Marcus: will do. I'll capture p95/p99 and queuing time.
[06:50] Tom: also please include cost delta for burst — we need to see unit economics.
[06:55] Samira: noted, I'll add cost breakdown to the addendum.
[07:00] Priya: re: security, one ask — can we get audit logs for prompt inputs? our compliance team needs redaction rules and retention policy.
[07:10] Jensen: yes we support configurable audit logging and KMS integration. we'll surface the retention controls in the docs and share SOC2 artifacts.
[07:20] Tom: and can we get a simple diagram for VPC peering and the private control plane options?
[07:26] Samira: yes we'll schedule the on-prem deep dive next week with infra team.
[07:32] Marcus: quick note on regression: a small subset of prompts consistently fail under high concurrency. hypothesize it's latency-induced internal timeout leading to truncated contexts.
[07:44] Ethan: we did see a bump in tail latency at peak traffic, might be threadpool saturation on our side — we'll check.
[07:50] Marcus: ok add that to the trial matrix, we'll run with higher concurrency to reproduce.
[07:58] Marta: question about evaluation: will the 1k run include both live and synthetic cases?
[08:03] Marcus: yes, we'll do a mixed dataset — 60% real, 40% synthetic fuzzed variants of the failing cases.
[08:12] Carlos: timeline recap please?
[08:16] Samira: Marcus runs regression and posts traces by 3/26, Samira sends addendum by 3/21, customer sends labeled prompts by 3/24, on-prem deep dive week of 3/28.
[08:30] Priya: sounds good. any blockers?
[08:33] Tom: none from execs, but want to see cost delta in writing.
[08:38] Samira: we'll include that. last question: do we want to loosen the guardrail now or after we see regression numbers?
[08:45] Marcus: suggest we relax guardrail for a small subset only and enable reranker as a safety net — low risk.
[08:55] Priya: ok let's do that for shipment_notes only.
[09:00] Samira: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in Slack and I'll circulate minutes plus the addendum.
[09:08] Jensen: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
